signals.title: USD/JPY — GEOPOLITICAL Escalation + Hawkish Fed Pivot
signals.text: The IRGC closure of the Strait of Hormuz and Chair Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole pivot (57% hike probability) drive safe-haven and yield-seeking flows into the USD open. USD/JPY closed at 160.04 Friday, but the bear flattener regime (2s10s +52bp) and JPY COT net short -81.61k (9th percentile) create significant squeeze risk if energy disruptions trigger a broad risk-off rotation. High US-JGB yield spreads (+179bp) provide structural support, though JPY 10Y yields at 2.93% and a positive JPY ESI (+20.1) signal domestic resistance. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY into the open; geopolitical shocks favor USD liquidity over JPY carry. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open — Strait of Hormuz closure headlines. Risk: Direct BoJ or MoF intervention triggered by the 160.00 breach.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + IRGC Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: AUD outperformance (1W avg +1.295%) vs CHF weakness (1W avg -0.623%) creates a 1.919% G10 spread that faces immediate exhaustion risk from the Strait of Hormuz closure. AUD/CHF carry (+435bp) and extreme retail shorting (95%) support the uptrend, but the pair is vulnerable to a safe-haven CHF reversal given the geopolitical Tier-1 event. AUD COT net long +53.5k (95th percentile) reflects a crowded long position susceptible to liquidation on risk-off headlines. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF from the open; geopolitical escalation favors laggard CHF recovery over crowded AUD longs. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open. Risk: Sustained risk-on sentiment if the Strait of Hormuz situation de-escalates rapidly.

signals.title: NZD/USD — RBNZ Hike Bias vs Crowded COT Short
signals.text: NZD COT LF net short -32.4k (0th percentile) represents the most crowded short in the G10, setting up a major squeeze ahead of the RBNZ meeting. The RBNZ hike bias (2 September) and neutral ESI (+2.6) contrast with the USD's -10.0 ESI, suggesting NZD resilience despite the hawkish Warsh speech. NZD/USD closed at 0.5913 Friday, remaining above its SMA20, SMA50, and SMA200, which confirms a bullish technical posture. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; record-crowded shorts face liquidation risk into the RBNZ decision. Catalyst: next RBNZ meeting (mkt: 94% hike priced) on 2 Sep. Risk: Geopolitical flight to USD liquidity overrides the RBNZ yield attraction.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Hawkish Fed vs Crowded COT Short
signals.text: EUR COT LF net short -55.3k (3rd percentile) and a -55.6k WoW decline signal an extreme bearish consensus following Chair Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole guidance. The EUR/USD closed at 1.1587, below its SMA20, as the Fed's 3.75% rate and 57% hike probability reinforce the +145bp OIS carry advantage for the USD. Despite positive EUR ESI (+12.7), the bear flattener regime in the US curve favors USD dominance. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; extreme COT short positioning limits further aggressive downside without a fresh catalyst. Catalyst: ECB meeting on 10 Sep. Risk: EUR short-squeeze if US economic data (NFP) misses expectations.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Carry Advantage vs Negative ESI
signals.text: GBP COT LF net long +56.8k (96th percentile) creates unwind risk as the BoE market bias remains on hold while the Fed shifts hawkish. Although GBP/USD carry favors GBP by 9bp (SONIA vs SOFR), a negative GBP ESI (-8.8) and moderate negative bias suggest fundamental data is lagging. The pair closed at 1.3534, hovering just below its SMA20 (1.354), indicating a loss of short-term momentum. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish GBP/USD; crowded long positioning is vulnerable to a hawkish Fed repricing. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 17 Sep. Risk: UK 10Y yield outperformance (5.15%) maintains the GBP bid against USD.
